look_here_first: Erect plant: inspect several stem nodes just BELOW the leaf stalk for a tiny spur-like TUBERCLE (not a true spine; it can be absent). Then inspect minute star-shaped hairs and, on mature fruit, five mericarps with paired short beaks. Flower color alone is not diagnostic.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: ovate to lanceolate leaves serrate toward the base

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: small spinelike tubercle often present below petiole

lookalikes.differences: Compare with Sida abutilifolia: spreading/procumbent stems and crenate leaves versus usually upright S. spinosa. Compare with Sida rhombifolia: often rhombic leaves with teeth concentrated distally; inspect multiple nodes for the characteristic small tubercle immediately below the petiole in S. spinosa. Absence of a visible tubercle in one photograph is not decisive. For confirmation inspect mature schizocarps: S. spinosa typically has five mericarps with two apical awns/beaks each; count and photograph the mericarps rather than relying on yellow flowers alone.
